PR #45595: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of parameter buffer allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45595

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR extends command-buffer virtual-address remapping to entry-computation parameter allocations. Parameter buffers remain caller-owned, so each execution aliases their physical memory into stable VA-reservation addresses instead of transferring ownership to the VMM allocator.

- Adds `ExecutionScope::ResolveParameterBuffer`; the base implementation returns the caller buffer, while the VA-remapping implementation installs and returns the stable reservation alias.
- Renames the `PrepareReservation` hook to `Prepare` and makes `ExecuteWithBufferAllocations` accept mutable `BufferAllocations`, allowing addresses to be restored after execution.
- Tracks per-execution parameter aliases with `RecordStepAlias`.
- Releases those aliases after every execution and rewrites remapped entries back to their caller-owned addresses before teardown and result handling. The execution-scope destructor provides cleanup for error paths.
- Adds `AddVaRemappedAllocationForTesting` and a host-only fake VMM allocator to exercise the parameter-remapping path without requiring a GPU.

This PR is stacked on #45567, **[XLA:GPU] Split command buffer VA remapping into its own allocator class**. It is part 1 of 3 splitting the former #45568 implementation into reviewable changes; #45596 adds output-buffer remapping and #45597 adds the `SKIP_PROFILED` mode.

## 🎯 Justification

`SKIP_TEMP` stabilizes only preallocated temporary buffers, but profiled command-buffer update policies also need to stabilize caller-owned parameters whose physical addresses remain constant across executions. Parameter ownership prevents allocating them directly through the command-buffer reservation.

Creating a per-execution alias gives recorded command buffers a stable VA while preserving the caller's original address and ownership. Restoring the original address after execution ensures teardown and result handling never observe a reservation address.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable as a standalone change. This PR adds parameter-remapping support but does not select it in a production update mode. Performance evaluation belongs to the final `SKIP_PROFILED` policy in #45597.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Added host-only `gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator_test.cc` coverage using a fake VMM allocator.
- Verifies that a caller-owned parameter receives the same stable reservation address across executions.
- Verifies persistent allocation-index handling, post-execution restoration to the caller address, and release of each per-execution mapping.
- Covers cleanup behavior without requiring a GPU.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

No standalone execution test is added because no production update mode selects parameter allocations in this PR. End-to-end selection and execution coverage is provided by the stacked `SKIP_PROFILED` change in #45597.

[XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of parameter buffer allocations

Allow command buffer VA remapping to give stable reservation addresses
to entry-computation-parameter allocations. Parameter buffers are owned
by the caller, so they are aliased into the VA reservation with Map()
each execution instead of being allocated through it:

- GpuExecutableBufferAllocator::ExecutionScope gains a
  ResolveParameterBuffer hook (base returns the caller buffer), and
  ExecuteWithBufferAllocations now takes a mutable BufferAllocations so
  subclasses can rewrite entries after execution. The Prepare hook is
  renamed from PrepareReservation.
- GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator records each installed alias
  (RecordStepAlias) and, after every execution, UnMaps the aliases and
  rewrites the remapped BufferAllocations entries back to the
  caller-owned addresses so TearDown and result handling never see
  reservation addresses (ReleaseStepAliases; the scope destructor is a
  safety net for error paths).
- No production update mode selects parameter allocations yet
  (SKIP_TEMP remaps only preallocated temp buffers); the
  AddVaRemappedAllocationForTesting seam plus a host-only fake VMM
  allocator (gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator_test.cc) exercise the
  new path: stable reservation address across executions, persistent
  allocation indices, post-execution rewrite, and mapping release.

Originally the pass was written for the Fusion Emitters pipeline. Now that it
is also used for CPU block codegen, we can have shaped types as well.

This change updates SimplifyArithPass to handle shaped types (vectors and
tensors) safely across several rewrite patterns:

  DenseElementsAttr constants when operating on ShapedType operands.

[PjRt-IFRT] Reject XLA HloShardingV3 (NamedSharding) format in IFRT `HloShardingSerDes` serialization

XLA `HloShardingV3` (NamedSharding) format is currently not version compatible across IFRT SerDes versions as the version compatibility contract has not been established around `HloShardingV3`, and `HloShardingV3` is intended to be used within the local XLA compiler. Allowing `HloShardingSerDes` to serialize `HloShardingV3` format can cause potential compatibility errors when communicating across different binary versions or using persistent artifacts such as model exports.

This change updates `HloShardingSerDes::Serialize` to explicitly reject `HloSharding` containing `HloShardingV3` format, returning an `InvalidArgumentError`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 948702212

[IFRT] Copy serialized Cord to std::string during deserialization to avoid ASan buffer overflow

MLIR Lexer (used by the text/assembly parser) assumes the input buffer is null-terminated.
When parsing text-based StableHLO during deserialization (e.g. on invalid input in tests), `deserializePortableArtifact` receives a non-null-terminated `absl::string_view` from `absl::Cord::Flatten()`.
If an identifier ends exactly at the buffer boundary, the lexer reads past the end of the buffer, causing an ASan `stack-buffer-overflow`.

To fix this safely, we copy the serialized data to a `std::string` to guarantee null-termination before passing it to MLIR parsing. Since this only happens during program deserialization (non-hot path), the performance impact is expected to be low, but we will need to do a follow-up if the extra cost turns out to be too high.

[PJRT] Add UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer: a hold-free PjRtBuffer for non-donating workloads.

Serving/inference buffers (like request inputs and loaded variables) follow a write-once, read-many lifecycle and are never donated. For these workloads, the hold-tracking and usage-event machinery in `CommonPjRtBuffer` causes unnecessary overhead and locking on the hot path.

`UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer` extends `xla::PjRtBuffer` directly and strips away this tracking state.

Key mechanics:
  * Safe Construction & RAII Lifetime:** Enforces non-null `raw_buffer` invariants upon construction. Buffer lifetime is strictly tied to C++ object destruction, deferring release (`DecrefAfter`) until all pending definition events resolve without tracking dormant utilization holds.
  * Lock-Free Accessors & Retrieval:** Because `raw_buffer_` stays valid throughout the C++ object's lifetime, `AcquireRawBufferRef()` and metadata accessors (`memory_space`, `device`, `client`) are completely lock-free (`mu_` is bypassed), avoiding mutex contention during high-throughput inference dispatch.
  * No-op `Delete()`:** `Delete()` is an explicit no-op (`IsDeleted()` returns `false`) and early release is disabled to prevent accidental use-after-delete races in asynchronous callbacks.

PR #45567: [XLA:GPU] Split command buffer VA remapping into its own allocator class

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45567

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR separates the command-buffer virtual-address remapping implementation from `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` into a dedicated `GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator` subclass. It is a structural refactor of the existing `SKIP_TEMP` behavior; no functional change is intended.

- `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` is now the common base implementation for allocation resolution and the `ALWAYS_UPDATE` policy. It also remains the runtime fallback for `SKIP_TEMP` when VA remapping is unavailable.
- `ExecutionScope` is now polymorphic and is returned as `std::unique_ptr<ExecutionScope>`. Protected hooks such as `PrepareReservation` and `AllocateTransientBuffer` provide the extension points needed by address-policy-specific subclasses.
- The new `GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator` owns the `SKIP_TEMP` implementation:
  - per-executor remapping state and synchronization;
  - deterministic VA reservation sizing and layout;
  - VMM-backed allocation of command-buffer-referenced temporary buffers;
  - persistent allocation indices combining constants with VA-remapped temporary allocations; and
  - synchronization of pending VMM operations during allocator teardown.
- `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator::Create` selects the base allocator for `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and the VA-remapping subclass for `SKIP_TEMP`.
- GPU executable and PJRT call sites now use the factory and pointer-owned execution scopes.
- The BUILD target includes the new source/header pair and retains the direct dependencies required by both implementations.
- VMM test logging now enables both allocator translation units so existing assertions continue to observe the VA-reservation messages after the code move.

This PR is stacked on #45130, **[XLA:GPU] Update command buffers when allocation policy changes**. The follow-up policy is implemented separately in #45568.

## 🎯 Justification

The base allocator previously mixed general buffer-allocation mechanics with one specific VMM address-stability policy. Splitting those responsibilities makes the default path easier to reason about and gives additional update policies a narrow place to implement reservation, allocation, and execution behavior without further expanding the base class.

This cleanup is primarily preparation for profiled command-buffer allocation policies. Existing GPU command-buffer workloads should retain the same `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and `SKIP_TEMP` behavior.

[XLA:GPU] Refactor DotMerger to use DotOperandDims and ShapeTracker.

This change enhances the capabilities of the DotMerger pass. Instead of relying on specific patterns like DotDecomposer's normal form, the new implementation uses `DotOperandDims` to track and categorize dimensions (Batch, Contracting, NonContracting) and `ShapeTracker` to generate the necessary transformation instructions (transpose, reshape, bitcast) to align operand shapes for merging.

Key improvements include:
-   Support for merging dots with different layouts on the shared or concatenated operands.
-   Ability to handle dots with arbitrary batch, contracting, and non-contracting dimension orders.
-   Merging of dots even when the non-shared operands have multiple non-contracting dimensions.
-   Improved handling of dependencies by merging only mutually unreachable dots within an equivalence class.
-   Simplification of consumer chains (transposes, reshapes, bitcasts) after the merged dot's output is sliced.

The equivalence classes are now built based on the shared operand's source instruction and the categorized dimensions at that source, allowing for more flexible grouping. The merging process involves transforming the operands to a common shape/layout before concatenation and then creating a single large dot. The results are then sliced and potentially transformed back to match the original dot outputs.

[xla:gpu] Improve dot fusion cost model by incorporating hardware launch waves

The existing pipelined loop cost model assumes perfect, continuous overlapping
between compute and memory operations. However, hardware executes in discrete
"waves" bounded by SM counts, available shared memory, and thread capacities.
When a kernel's resource requirements prevent all threadblocks from launching
simultaneously, the pipeline is interrupted at wave boundaries, causing overhead.

This CL introduces hardware wave awareness into the pipelined cost model to
prevent it from under-predicting the execution time of configurations that
require multiple waves.

Key changes:
* Abstract a new `CalculateHardwareLaunchWaves` metric to predict the number
  of discrete execution waves, accounting for shared memory and warp occupancy
  limits across physical SMs.
* Introduce `CalculatePipelinedLoopTimeWithLaunchWaves`, which applies the
  pipelined execution model on a per-wave basis. This models the pipeline
  drain/fill overhead at wave boundaries.
* Iron out precision drops and mitigate potential divide-by-zero hazards when
  evaluating degenerate 0-block layouts.
* Add unit tests to explicitly verify wave computation scaling and assert the
  correctness of per-wave pipeline bounding logic across different memory limits.

PR #44403: [XLA:CPU] onednn_threadpool: cap num_workers at n in parallel_for

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44403

📝 Summary of Changes
`OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for` (xla/backends/cpu/runtime/onednn/onednn_threadpool.h)  was passing `thread_pool_- NumThreads()` as `num_workers` regardless of `n`. Before   #42581, `Worker::Parallelize` had an entry-point clamp (`num_workers = std::min(num_work_items, num_workers)`) that silently fixed this up. #42581 replaced that clamp with a branch that triggers when `num_workers > num_work_items`:

  ```cpp
  if (num_workers > num_work_items) {
    num_partitions = ceil(num_work_items / 8);
    num_workers   = std::min(num_workers, num_partitions);
  }
  ```

  For oneDNN's small-n dispatches (reorders, packing, eltwise/softmax tiles), this collapses parallelism to ceil(n/8) cores.
  eg: On a 56-thread host, n = 20 drops from 20 active cores to 3; n <= 8 falls through to a fully serial fallback. Multiplied across the many small primitives, this causes significant regression across multiple models when built with `build_with_onednn_async=true` and `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_cpu_experimental_onednn_custom_call=true`

  Fix
  Cap num_workers at n at the caller, matching the pattern already used in xla/backends/cpu/runtime/kernel.cc and xla/backends/cpu/runtime/convolution_lib.h:
  ```cpp
  const size_t num_workers = std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(n),
                                              thread_pool_->NumThreads());
  ```

  With num_workers <= num_work_items, the call takes the else branch (num_partitions = num_workers) and behaves like pre-#42581. For n >= NumThreads(), the cap is a no-op and the heap/cacheline win from #42581 is fully preserved.

🎯 Justification
It fixes the significant regression (25%-60%) across multiple models run on CPU with onednn

PR #45130: [XLA:GPU] Trigger command buffers update when persistent allocations set changed.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45130

For command buffer run, add the required processing for allowing `persistent_alloc_indices` to transition only from absent to present across execution steps and must remain unchanged once present.

We may require this transition because the chosen of buffer allocations whose address are in `persistent_alloc_indices` might not be available from the first step, e.g, if persistent allocations are only available after several steps of profiling.  So we need to make sure that command buffer is correctly updated when `persistent_alloc_indices` is changed across steps.

📝 Summary of Changes

- Document that `persistent_alloc_indices` may transition only from absent to
  present across execution steps and must remain unchanged once present.
- Track only whether persistent-allocation information was valid when each
  executor's command buffer was recorded, avoiding an owned vector copy and
  repeated value comparisons.
- Force a full command-buffer update in `CommandBufferThunk::Initialize` when
  persistent allocation information first becomes valid.
- In `ExecuteOnStream`, recover from a recorded/current information-validity
  mismatch by fully updating the command buffer. This covers a
  profiling-skipped update and interleaving with an older execution initialized
  before policy activation.
- Use the public `ShapedSlice` header and its direct BUILD dependency.

🎯 Justification

The persistent allocation policy controls which recorded addresses a command
buffer can safely retain. When the policy first becomes available, an
allocation-filtered update can skip a command whose allocations are now all
persistent, leaving stale addresses in the command buffer. A full update fixes
that transition.

Although the policy transition is logically one-way, executions initialized on
opposite sides of it can interleave on the shared per-executor command buffer.
An Execute-time validity check therefore forces a full update for either
recorded/current mismatch without comparing policy vectors on every step.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A. This is a correctness fix.

🧪 Unit Tests:

Extended `PersistentAllocIndicesBecomingAvailableTriggersUpdate` to verify:

- absent-to-present activation during Initialize triggers exactly one update;
- Execute recovers when the initialization update was skipped;
- an older absent-policy execution and the following present-policy execution
  each restore the correct recorded addresses when they interleave.

Also ran `GpuExecutableTest.CommandBufferAllocationPolicy`.

🧪 Execution Tests:

Ran the focused command-buffer regression and allocation-policy test with
Bazel. All seven configured GPU architecture variants of
`command_buffer_thunk_test` passed, and `gpu_executable_test` passed.

PR #45559: [HLO] Return parse errors instead of CHECK-failing on malformed replica_groups=mesh[...]

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45559

### Problem
The HLO text parser aborts (via `CHECK`/`CHECK_EQ`) instead of returning a parse error on a malformed `replica_groups=mesh[...]` collective-device list. Because these come straight from user-provided HLO text (`ParseAndReturnUnverifiedModule` and friends), a malformed axis reference or device-id list crashes the process rather than producing a diagnostic. Three sites in `ParseAxisRef`/`ParseMesh`:

1. **Invalid axis ref** — `CHECK(absl::SimpleAtoi(axis_name_or_index, &axis_index))` fires when the axis reference is neither a known mesh axis name nor an integer:
   ```
   replica_groups=mesh['axis_0'=2,'axis_1'=2] {'bogus'}
   ```
2. **Axis index out of bounds** — `CHECK(axis_index >= 0 && axis_index < mesh.axis_names().size())` fires on an out-of-range (or negative) index:
   ```
   replica_groups=mesh['axis_0'=2,'axis_1'=2] {'5'}
   ```
3. **device_ids count mismatch** — `CHECK_EQ(devices.size(), device_ids_array.num_elements())` fires when the `device_ids=(...)` count doesn't match the mesh size:
   ```
   replica_groups=mesh['axis_0'=2,'axis_1'=2, device_ids=(0,1,2)] {'axis_0'}
   ```
   The `Array<int64_t>` is also constructed (allocating the product of the axis sizes) *before* the check, so a huge mesh with a mismatched device list can attempt an unbounded allocation.

### Fix
Return a `TokenError` from each site instead of `CHECK`-failing, matching how the rest of the parser reports malformed input. For (3), the device-id count is validated against an overflow-checked product of the axis sizes *before* the `Array` is allocated, so a mismatched or overflowing mesh yields a parse error rather than a bad-alloc or abort.

Valid `mesh[...]` lists are unaffected (the existing `AllReduceWithMeshAxesReplicaGroupList` round-trip test still passes).

### Tests
Three `HloParserTest` cases assert the malformed inputs above now return an error status instead of crashing.

---
Disclosure: this contribution was authored with an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed before submission.

[XLA:GPU] Refactor DotMerger to use DotOperandDims and ShapeTracker.

This change enhances the capabilities of the DotMerger pass. Instead of relying on specific patterns like DotDecomposer's normal form, the new implementation uses `DotOperandDims` to track and categorize dimensions (Batch, Contracting, NonContracting) and `ShapeTracker` to generate the necessary transformation instructions (transpose, reshape, bitcast) to align operand shapes for merging.

Key improvements include:
-   Support for merging dots with different layouts on the shared or concatenated operands.
-   Ability to handle dots with arbitrary batch, contracting, and non-contracting dimension orders.
-   Merging of dots even when the non-shared operands have multiple non-contracting dimensions.
-   Improved handling of dependencies by merging only mutually unreachable dots within an equivalence class.
-   Simplification of consumer chains (transposes, reshapes, bitcasts) after the merged dot's output is sliced.

The equivalence classes are now built based on the shared operand's source instruction and the categorized dimensions at that source, allowing for more flexible grouping. The merging process involves transforming the operands to a common shape/layout before concatenation and then creating a single large dot. The results are then sliced and potentially transformed back to match the original dot outputs.

PR #45401: [HLO] Rewrite a scalar-operand gather to a broadcast in GatherSimplifier

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45401

### Problem
`GatherSimplifier` crashed on a gather from a scalar (rank-0) operand: such a gather has empty `offset_dims`, which `IsSimplifiedGather` dereferenced out of bounds (and the pass could otherwise loop without making progress).

### Fix
Rather than treating a scalar-operand gather as already-simplified (which just skips it), eliminate it — mirroring `ScatterSimplifier`:
- `IsSimplifiedGather` returns `false` for a rank-0 operand (`operand_rank == 0`), which also avoids the out-of-bounds `offset_dims` dereference.
- `ExpandInstruction` rewrites a rank-0-operand gather into a `broadcast` of the scalar operand to the result shape (matching the existing zero-slice-size → broadcast path), so the gather is removed instead of being left in place.

Behavior is unchanged for all other gathers.

### Test
`RewritesScalarOperandGatherToBroadcast` asserts a scalar-operand gather is rewritten to `broadcast(%operand), dimensions={}`.

Lower xtile.scan to Triton.

This change introduces a pattern to transform `xtile::ScanOp` into `ttir::ScanOp`. There are three gaps to bridge:

- `xtile.scan` supports initial values, but `tt.scan` does not. So we need to broadcast them and add them to the result of `tt.scan`.
- Finally, `tt.scan` does not return final carry values. We extract them by slicing the scan result.

The change also introduces support for left-masking `xtile.extract/insert`. This is needed for reverse scan when the tile size is not a multiple of the scan dimension size.

PR #45398: [GPU] Fix out-of-bounds read in AllReduceSplitter ReplicaGroups comparator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45398

### Problem
`AllReduceSplitter`'s `ReplicaGroups` dedup comparator reads out of bounds (and can report distinct replica-group sets as equal) when two all-reduces have the same number of groups but different per-group sizes.

### Root cause
```cpp
friend H AbslHashValue(H h, const ReplicaGroups& rg) {
  return H::combine(std::move(h), rg.replica_groups.size());   // only the group COUNT
}
friend bool operator==(const ReplicaGroups& item, const ReplicaGroups& other) {
  if (item.replica_groups.size() != other.replica_groups.size()) return false;
  for (int i = 0; i < item.replica_groups.size(); i++) {
    const ReplicaGroup& item_replica_group = item.replica_groups[i];
    const ReplicaGroup& other_replica_group = other.replica_groups[i];
    for (int i = 0; i < item_replica_group.replica_ids_size(); i++) {   // bound = item's size
      if (item_replica_group.replica_ids(i) != other_replica_group.replica_ids(i))  // indexes OTHER
        return false;
```
The inner loop is bounded by `item`'s group size but dereferences `other.replica_ids(i)`, with **no per-group size-equality check**. `RunImpl` calls `GetReplicaGroupsMap` unconditionally on every computation and inserts every all-reduce into a `flat_hash_map` keyed by `ReplicaGroups`, so this comparator runs for any two all-reduces with the same group count. The HLO verifier explicitly allows non-uniform replica-group sizes for all-reduce, so e.g. `{{0,1},{2,3}}` vs `{{0,1,2},{3}}` (both 2 groups) collide on the degenerate hash and the comparator reads `replica_ids(2)` past a size-2 `RepeatedField` — an out-of-bounds read (DCHECK/ASan abort, UB in release). In the reverse order it returns a false "equal" (prefix match), corrupting the split heuristic.

The sibling reassociate passes compare full `replica_groups` element- and size-wise via `AllReduceKey`.

### Fix
Add the missing per-group size-equality check before the inner loop (fixes the OOB and the false-equal), and hash the actual `replica_ids` instead of only the group count so semantically different groups don't all share one bucket.

### Test
`HandlesAllReducesWithNonUniformReplicaGroupsOfSameCount`: two all-reduces with 2 groups each but different per-group sizes; building the map no longer reads out of bounds (previously an ASan/DCHECK abort).

```cpp
          group.elements.size());
  broadcast = body->AddInstruction(
      HloInstruction::CreateReshape(data_shape, broadcast));
}
```

`operand_inserted_concat_dim` is a `bool`. Using it as the argument to `dimensions()` reads dimension `0` (since `false == 0`) instead of the concat dimension. The new dimension size is therefore computed from the wrong dimension. When `dimensions(operand_concat_dim) != dimensions(0)`, the reshaped shape has a different element count than the broadcast, and `CreateReshape` fails its `ShapeUtil::ElementsIn` `CHECK`, aborting compilation.

The intended value is the concat dimension's own size, which is exactly the dimension being overwritten by `set_dimensions(operand_concat_dim, ...)`.

### Fix
Read the size of `operand_concat_dim`, not dimension 0:

```cpp
data_shape.set_dimensions(
    operand_concat_dim,
    data_shape.dimensions(operand_concat_dim) * group.elements.size());
```

When the concat is on dimension 0 (the case the existing tests cover) the two indices coincide, so this is a no-op there and only corrects the non-zero-dimension case.

### Test
`SharedBroadcastOperandNonZeroConcatDim`: a while loop whose body concatenates two `f32[3,5]` group elements on dimension 1 and feeds each through an `add` with a shared operand. The shared operand takes the broadcast+reshape path; under the old code the reshape targets `f32[3,6]` (18 elements) from a `f32[3,2,5]` broadcast (30 elements) and crashes. With the fix it reshapes to `f32[3,10]` and partitioning succeeds.

PR #45312: [ROCm] Allow asynchronous deallocation for StreamExecutorAddressAllocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45312

### 📝 Summary of Changes
Report `AllowsAsynchronousDeallocation() == true` for
`StreamExecutorAddressAllocator` **on the ROCM platform only**, and drop the
now-obsolete synchronous-only `CHECK` in `GetStream()`. With this,
`OwningScratchAllocator` frees scratch inline instead of deferring it into a
`Stream::DoHostCallback`. CUDA and SYCL keep their prior behavior.

### 🎯 Justification
On ROCm the synchronous free calls `hipFree`, which deadlocks when invoked
from a HIP stream-callback thread. `OwningScratchAllocator` only defers the
free into a host callback for allocators reporting async-dealloc == false, so
any op allocating a work buffer hangs — notably real FFTs
(`rfft`/`irfft`/`hfft`/`ihfft`/`rfft2`) under the address allocator on gfx950,
which blocked the JAX ROCm test suite at the FFT stage. `Deallocate()` uses
`hipFree`, which already synchronizes the device, so deallocation is safe to
issue asynchronously; reporting `true` frees scratch inline (off the callback)
and keeps the path non-blocking, matching the VMM allocators.

This is scoped to the ROCM platform. CUDA's `cuMemFree` is also
device-synchronizing and would be safe, but SYCL's `sycl::free` synchronizes
only the passed queue (not all device queues), so returning `true` there could
free memory still in use on another queue. CUDA and SYCL therefore retain
their existing behavior.

`GetStream()` is also used by the autotuner/profiler regardless of dealloc
mode, so its `!AllowsAsynchronousDeallocation()` CHECK is removed.

### 🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

### 🧪 Unit Tests:
None. The deadlock is ROCm-GPU-specific (`hipFree` in a HIP callback); on the
host/CPU platform `DoHostCallback` runs fine, so a CPU unit test cannot
reproduce it and would pass with or without the change.

### 🧪 Execution Tests:
Covered by existing JAX ROCm FFT tests (`fft_test.py`, `scipy_fft_test.py`)
run under `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=address`: real-transform cases hang
without this fix and pass with it (verified on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2.0).

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45062

Stacked on #44296. This PR should be reviewed and merged after #44296.

Currently, `NEVER_UPDATE` and `CAPTURE_CMD_NEVER_UPDATE` mode is to avoid graph update through VMM memory allocator's VA-remapping, but it seems that they are not not always work well for  all workloads. So  this PR want to clean the va-remap mode and make the va-remap mode more conservative (just introduce mode with confident speedup) by only allowing va-remapping for TEMP buffer.

📝 Summary of Changes

- Define two command-buffer update modes: `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and `SKIP_TEMP`.
- Treat referenced constants as persistent in both modes.
- In `SKIP_TEMP`, give command-buffer-referenced preallocated temporary buffers stable VMM reservation addresses while parameters and live-out buffers remain dynamically updated.
- Collect the persistent and VA-remapped allocation indices once when `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` is instantiated, and pass the resulting persistent vector directly to command-buffer execution.
- Remove the former address-policy mode state, redundant checks, dead accessors, and the intermediate allocation-index collection API.
- Document allocator selection, non-VMM fallback, and the resulting address policy.

🎯 Justification

Command buffers can avoid unnecessary address updates for executable-owned temporary buffers when those buffers retain stable virtual addresses. Restricting VMM remapping to preallocated temporaries preserves the caller's normal parameter and output allocation semantics. The simplified allocator state also makes the fallback and remapping behavior easier to follow and maintain.

PR #45402: [SPMD] Fall back when FFT halo exchange is not possible

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45402

### Problem
The SPMD FFT handler aborts the compiler (`CHECK_EQ`) when halo exchange can't be performed for the sharded FFT dimension.

### Root cause
```cpp
auto result = partitioned_input.hlo();
auto padded_hlo = PadEachPartitionWithHaloExchange(...);
if (padded_hlo.has_value()) {
  result = padded_hlo.value();
}
// falls through even when padded_hlo == nullopt (result stays un-padded)
result = ShuffleWithinEachPartitionUsingOneHot(result, num_partitions_, ...);
```
`PadEachPartitionWithHaloExchange` returns `std::nullopt` only when the per-shard size is **not** a multiple of `num_partitions` (padding is exactly what would make it divisible). When it returns `nullopt`, `HandleFft` ignores it and proceeds with the un-padded operand into `ShuffleWithinEachPartitionUsingOneHot`, whose `CHECK_EQ(size_per_partition % num_partitions, 0)` then fires — so a `nullopt` return *always* aborts the compiler.

This is reachable from verifier-valid HLO: an FFT whose last dimension is sharded down to a per-shard size too small to gather the halo, e.g. `fft(c64[1,1,2]), fft_length={2}, sharding={devices=[1,1,2]}` (per-shard size 1, halo length 2). The nullopt is returned inside `ExchangeHalo` (`max_right_halo_size > input_shard_size`).

### Fix
Treat a `nullopt` from `PadEachPartitionWithHaloExchange` as unsupported and return `DefaultAction(hlo)` — the replicated fallback the handler already uses for its other unsupported FFT cases — instead of proceeding with the un-padded operand.

### Test
`Fft3DSmallShardFallsBack`: an FFT with a per-shard size of 1 now partitions successfully (previously a `CHECK` abort).

PR #45332: [ROCm] Fall back to library collective for non-uniform replica groups

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45332

The collective (one-shot/two-shot) AllReduce kernel bakes the clique size (world_size) as a compile-time constant from the first replica group and sizes its signal/staging buffers the same way. With non-uniform replica groups (e.g. axis_index_groups=[[0,1],[2,3,4,5,6,7]]) the single emitted kernel runs on cliques of different sizes, causing out-of-bounds peer accesses (GPU page fault) and hangs on gfx950.

Reject the collective kernel when replica groups differ in size so the op falls back to the library (RCCL/NCCL) collective, which handles heterogeneous cliques. Uniform replica groups are unaffected.

## 📝 Summary of Changes
Add a uniformity guard to `IsAllReduceKernelSupported` (`xla/backends/gpu/runtime/all_reduce.cc`): if any replica group's size differs from the first group's size, the custom collective AllReduce kernel is not selected and the op falls back to the library (RCCL/NCCL) collective. No device-code changes; uniform replica groups continue to use the kernel unchanged.

## 🎯 Justification
The collective kernel's clique size (`world_size`) is a codegen-time constant taken from the first replica group, and its signal/staging buffers are sized the same way. A single AllReduce with non-uniform replica groups therefore emits one kernel that is then run across cliques of *different* sizes, which reads/writes past the per-rank buffers → GPU page fault (`SQC` client, addr `0x0`) and/or a wedged HSA queue and hang. This is observed on ROCm/gfx950 with e.g. `pmap` + `axis_index_groups=[[0,1],[2,3,4,5,6,7]]`. Any workload that issues an AllReduce over uneven replica groups is affected; the kernel is architecturally single-clique-size, so falling back to the library collective (which handles heterogeneous cliques) is the correct behavior.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A — this is a correctness fix. It only diverts non-uniform-group AllReduces (which are broken today) to the library collective; uniform-group AllReduces still use the custom kernel, so no performance change for supported cases.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:
No new unit test in this commit. A targeted addition would be an assertion that `IsAllReduceKernelSupported(...)` returns an `Unimplemented` status for a replica-group set with differing group sizes (e.g. `{{0,1},{2,3,4,5}}`) and remains supported for uniform groups — happy to add this if desired.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:
Covered by the existing `tests/pmap_test.py::PythonPmapTest::testPsumUnevenReplicaGroups`, which exercises uneven `axis_index_groups` and previously hung. Note this cannot be expressed within the "at most 2 GPUs" guidance: non-uniform replica groups require at least 3 devices (two groups of different sizes), and the test itself skips when `device_count <= 2`. Validated on 8x MI355X (gfx950) with the kernel enabled: full ROCm UT suite passes — single-accelerator `29118 passed` (1 pre-existing unrelated DLPack waiver), multi-accelerator `854 passed, 0 failed` (previously wedged at this test). Path confirmed via VLOG: uneven groups → 0 kernel launches / all RCCL; even groups → kernel used.

PR #45070: [ROCm] [xla:gpu]VMM command-buffer: skip-remap + copy-into-shadow for launch-bound regimes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45070

## Summary
This one followed by #44726 as optimization:

Optimize the ROCm VMM command-buffer VA-remapping path (`ExecuteWithVaRemapping`) so that trace-once capture + replay (`NEVER_UPDATE`) is a net win in launch-bound (tensor-parallel) regimes, where the per-step VA remap previously outweighed the benefit.

The optimization is based on two properties of the per-step remap on ROCm:

- Most command-buffer slots (model weights) keep the same backing physical buffer across steps, yet the existing path unmapped and re-mapped the entire reservation every step — and on ROCm `hipMemUnmap` is the dominant per-step cost.
- A small number of tiny slices (scale/scalar/metric buffers) change address every step and are the worst case for remapping (a full unmap/map/SetAccess round-trip costs milliseconds even for a few bytes).

Two ROCm-gated changes; the CUDA path and the default ROCm behavior are unchanged:

1. **Skip-remap** — cache each slot's source (BFC) address and only remap the slots whose backing buffer actually moved, reusing the in-tree, unit-tested `se::MemoryReservation::ScopedMapping::Remap()`. In steady state (nothing moved) it issues zero driver calls and skips the unmap-event sync. Default ON for ROCm; set `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_vmm_skip_remap=false` to force the legacy path for A/B.
2. **Copy-into-shadow** — keep tiny churning slices out of the contiguous reservation and give each a stable shadow buffer (fixed address baked into the replayed command buffer), refreshed each step with a stream-ordered D2D copy instead of a remap. Opt-in via `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_vmm_copy_threshold_bytes` (bytes; `0` = default, disabled).

Both knobs are standard XLA flags (`xla.proto` / `DebugOptions`), not environment variables; they are read from the module's `DebugOptions` and only take effect on ROCm.

## Performance

Measured with MaxText (synthetic data, identical converged loss across configurations). Numbers are **relative per-step speedups** (steady-state median, after warm-up), **normalized to the default baseline configuration**; absolute throughput is omitted. Each model compares the default baseline config against the VMM-optimized config (trace-once replay + collectives captured + per-step remap minimized). Baseline = `1.00×`; higher is faster.

### 8×MI300X

| model       | baseline (default) | VMM-optimized |
| ----------- | :----------------: | :-----------: |
| llama2-7b   | 1.00×              | 1.09×         |
| llama3-8b   | 1.00×              | 1.16×         |
| llama3.1-8b | 1.00×              | 1.17×         |
| mistral-7b  | 1.00×              | 1.14×         |

a407b1298a594be9eb887afbd6f0868c4b8415fc by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Skip remapping unchanged command-buffer VA slots

The VA-remapping command-buffer path (ExecuteWithVaRemapping) unmapped the
entire reserved VA range and re-mapped every command-buffer allocation on
every step, even though most slots (model weights) keep the same backing
physical buffer step-to-step. On ROCm the VA unmap is the dominant per-step
cost, so this full remap is wasteful.

Wire the already-in-tree, unit-tested se::MemoryReservation::ScopedMapping::
Remap() per-slice skip primitive into the per-step path: cache each slot's
source (BFC) address from the previous step and mark remap_required only for
slots whose backing buffer moved. Unchanged slots keep their mapping (no
unmap/map/SetAccess), and when nothing changed the unmap-event sync is skipped
entirely (steady state issues zero driver calls).

ROCm-gated (VmmRemapSkipEnabled); the CUDA path keeps its existing
reset()+MapTo behavior. XLA_VMM_SKIP_REMAP=0 forces the legacy path for A/B.

Measured (8xMI300X, FSDP=8, 8 layers, NEVER_UPDATE, 30 steps), median ms/step:
  llama2-7b: 1096.5 -> 552.0  (1.99x)
  llama3-8b: 1284.0 -> 616.0  (2.08x)
Identical converged loss; no crash.

--
ffecfda0301f1ccd7a2db64f60ae2373bcd14bec by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Copy-into-shadow for small command-buffer VA slots

Small command-buffer slices (tiny scale/scalar/metric buffers that churn
their address every step) are the worst case for VMM per-step remapping: a
full hipMemUnmap/hipMemMap/hipMemSetAccess round-trip costs ~2-4ms even for a
few bytes, and there can be many such slices per step.

This change keeps those slices OUT of the contiguous VA reservation and instead
gives each a stable shadow device buffer (allocated once, fixed address baked
into the replayed command buffer). Each step the shadow is refreshed with a
stream-ordered D2D copy (real->shadow before execute, shadow->real after) rather
than a remap. Gated by XLA_VMM_TMP_COPY_THRESHOLD (bytes; 0 = disabled, default),
ROCm-only, so the CUDA path and default ROCm behavior are unchanged.

Combined with the per-slot skip-remap, this makes capturing collectives into the
command buffer (NEVER_UPDATE) a net win in launch-bound (tensor-parallel) regimes.
Loss/correctness unchanged.

0c3bcb527fc8f70f42736b5197edcbc79365dc36 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address review on VMM skip-remap + copy-into-shadow

Fixes from the PR #1001 review of the copy-into-shadow path:

- Fix shadow-buffer leak: VaRanges now stores its owning StreamExecutor and a
  destructor frees every small_shadow DeviceAddressBase (non-owning pointers
  were previously never deallocated). VaRanges is marked non-copyable.
- Avoid a use-after-free race when a shadow slot grows: synchronize the
  unmap_event before deallocating the old (still possibly GPU-referenced)
  shadow buffer.
- Allocate the shadow in the original buffer's memory space (color) instead of
  always memory_space=0, so a non-default-color slice is not silently misplaced.
- XLA_VMM_TMP_COPY_THRESHOLD now warns on empty/non-numeric values (e.g.
  "auto") instead of silently parsing to 0 via strtoull.
- Extract the env-var decision logic into pure, uncached vmm_internal helpers
  and add gpu_executable_buffer_allocator_test.cc covering them.

ROCm-gated; CUDA path and default ROCm behavior unchanged.

--
02f77c60874ef4f5d7953454afb5eb1982d2f475 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address second review round on copy-into-shadow

- Fail loudly when a copy-into-shadow slice grows after first capture: under
  trace-once replay (NEVER_UPDATE) the shadow address is baked into the command
  buffer and cannot move, so reallocating would silently corrupt the replayed
  buffer. Return an error instead of reallocating (also removes the prior
  dealloc/realloc + GPU-race path). Static shapes never hit this.
- Return an error if a command-buffer slice index is out of range instead of
  silently defaulting the shadow's memory space to 0.
- Make XLA_VMM_SKIP_REMAP parsing case-insensitive for false/off/no via
  absl::EqualsIgnoreCase; extend the unit test accordingly.
- Document that the small-slice copy is intentionally bidirectional (direction-
  agnostic, tiny buffers); note a future BufferUse-based optimization.

Note: the reviewer's "Internal() uses StrCat" comment is a false positive --
xla::Internal is absl::StrFormat-based (xla/util.h), so %d is substituted.

ROCm-gated; CUDA path and default ROCm behavior unchanged.

--
b3a577e0c51ce8aaf07130941ac4d2c7aa0d28c0 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address round-2 review on VMM skip-remap + copy-into-shadow

Fixes from the second claude-review pass on PR #1001:

- Skip-remap: if ScopedMapping::Remap() fails, reset scoped_mapping before
  returning the error. Remap() consumes the mapping via std::move, so leaving
  the (now moved-from) optional with has_value()==true would make the next
  step's skip path call Remap() on an empty mapping (UB). Resetting forces the
  legacy reset()+MapTo() recovery path instead.
- VaRanges destructor: synchronize unmap_event before deallocating the shadow
  buffers. The last step's command buffer may still be using them on the
  device, and hipFree on in-use memory is UB on ROCm. Marked
  ABSL_NO_THREAD_SAFETY_ANALYSIS (runs at teardown, no other thread present).
- Add ABSL_GUARDED_BY(mutex) to the mutex-protected VaRanges fields
  (va_reservation, unmap_event, scoped_mapping, last_mapped_src_addrs,
  small_shadow) so the thread-safety analyzer enforces the locking.
- Debug-only DCHECK that the per-slot reservation offsets are stable across
  steps, making the skip-remap "same allocation per slot" invariant explicit
  (new last_mapped_offsets companion vector, populated only in non-NDEBUG).
- ParseVmmRemapSkipEnabled: treat empty XLA_VMM_SKIP_REMAP the same as unset
  (default ON), matching ParseVmmCopyThresholdBytes; add a unit test.

ROCm-gated; CUDA path and default ROCm behavior unchanged.

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Gate VMM skip-remap/copy-into-shadow via DebugOptions flags

Address upstream review: don't read environment variables directly. Replace
the XLA_VMM_SKIP_REMAP / XLA_VMM_TMP_COPY_THRESHOLD getenv reads with standard
XLA flags in xla.proto / DebugOptions.

- xla.proto: add xla_gpu_command_buffer_vmm_skip_remap (bool, default true) and

- gpu_executable_buffer_allocator: drop the getenv-based env parsers and the
  process-static caches; read the flag values from the module's DebugOptions

  vmm_internal helpers now apply only the ROCm-only gating (and clamp a
  negative threshold to 0) so they stay unit-testable.
- Update the unit test to cover the flag-based helpers.

307a8d51129ef732345ff4cd6f2d8b491b393cb2 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address review: experimental flags + split ExecuteWithVaRemapping

Rename the two VMM command-buffer knobs with the xla_gpu_experimental_ prefix
(xla_gpu_experimental_command_buffer_vmm_skip_remap and
xla_gpu_experimental_command_buffer_vmm_copy_threshold_bytes); they are meant to
fold into the default behavior and be removed, so they are not a stable contract.
Field numbers are unchanged.

Break the ~400-line ExecuteWithVaRemapping into a thin orchestrator plus five
helpers on ExecutionScope: EnsureVaReservation, ComputeReservationOffsets,
GetOrCreateSmallShadow, BuildStepMappingPlan and EstablishMapping. Behavior is
unchanged; the per-executor mutex contract is preserved via
ABSL_EXCLUSIVE_LOCKS_REQUIRED and the allocator unit test still passes.

279ab0076a19ce2e1846105c1f83cb8434fe134d by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Always maintain last_mapped_offsets (drop #ifndef NDEBUG)

The per-slot reservation-offset bookkeeping used by the skip-remap DCHECK was
guarded by #ifndef NDEBUG to keep the release hot path free of the work. Measured
in isolation (-O2 -DNDEBUG) the maintenance is ~10-150 ns per step at typical
command-buffer slot counts (tens to hundreds), <=0.3 us at 512 slots, and N*8
bytes of RAM -- negligible next to the microsecond-to-millisecond
hipMemUnmap/hipMemMap it sits beside. Drop the preprocessor guard and always
populate it for readability; the DCHECK is still compiled out in release.

63638b5ac1835becd46d85af4498a8935f58df5a by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Temporarily disable collective command-buffer capture under VMM to fix numerical correctness

Under the VMM VA-remapping command-buffer update modes (NEVER_UPDATE /
CAPTURE_CMD_NEVER_UPDATE) a collective is traced into the command buffer once
and then replayed. On ROCm the traced RCCL collective binds its buffers at
trace time and does not follow the per-step physical remap / copy-into-shadow
refresh; additionally, on multi-GPU its cross-rank data-ready synchronization
is not re-established on HIP-graph replay (replay re-runs only the GPU kernel,
not RCCL's host-side proxy work-counter progression). The replayed collective
therefore reads stale buffers and silently corrupts results whenever the
collective's buffers churn across steps (e.g. TP/FSDP training; observed as
space_TP=8 loss divergence).

As a temporary correctness fix, do not convert collectives to command buffers
on ROCm in these VMM update modes -- run them eagerly instead. All
non-collective ops (fusions, gemms, custom-calls) remain captured. This trades
the collective-capture performance benefit for correctness until RCCL supports
graph-replay-safe collectives (fully kernel-driven intra-node collectives, or
replay-safe symmetric / user-buffer registration).

ALWAYS_UPDATE re-records the collective each step and is unaffected.
NVIDIA/CUDA behaviour is unchanged (ROCm-gated).

8e3914d7bae5da7660d8b7a4e09943910e2a2b64 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

Fix xla.proto field-number collision surfaced by the merge

The textual auto-merge of xla/xla.proto left the PR's two ROCm VMM flags at
DebugOptions field numbers 505/506, which upstream's main-mirror history had
meanwhile assigned to xla_gpu_cudnn_deviceless_compilation_mode (505) and
xla_gpu_enable_nccl_user_buffers_in_default_space (506). protoc rejected the
duplicate field numbers. Renumber the PR flags to the next free numbers:
  xla_gpu_experimental_command_buffer_vmm_skip_remap: 505 -> 507
  xla_gpu_experimental_command_buffer_vmm_copy_threshold_bytes: 506 -> 508
and update the stale "Next id" comment (512 is in use) to 513.

b4aebe0c2a49b2bbc1af985a6031b7c0e4bfd909 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

Resolve merge: port PR VMM allocator to upstream persistent-index API

The origin/main-mirror merge conflicts in gpu_executable_buffer_allocator.
{cc,h} were overlapping rewrites: the PR's ROCm-safe VMM command-buffer
allocator (whole-range VA reservation + skip-remap + copy-into-shadow) vs
~163 upstream commits that refactored the allocator around a new
`persistent_alloc_indices` command-buffer mechanism and a ThunkExecutor*
constructor.

Resolution keeps the PR's ROCm-safe VA-remap/copy-shadow implementation
byte-for-byte (upstream's per-allocation partial-range hipMemSetAccess path
crashes on ROCm) and adapts it to upstream's interface:
- Add CommandBufferAllocationIndexes { persistent, va_remapped }; collect both
  in CollectCommandBufferAllocationIndexes (constants -> persistent only;
  non-constant command allocs -> both).
- Constructor takes ThunkExecutor* and collects the index sets internally.
- ExecuteWithBufferAllocations / ExecuteWithVaRemapping thread
  persistent_alloc_indices through the execute callback so the command-buffer
  thunk traces once and skips per-step updates for stable (reserved-VA/shadow)
  addresses; GetPersistentAllocIndices() returns nullopt when the scope is not
  driving VMM remapping (legacy behavior).
- All VA-remap internals (EnsureVaReservation, ComputeReservationOffsets,
  BuildStepMappingPlan, CreateExecutionScope) now iterate the va_remapped set.

Pure-VMM correctness preserved: 1-GPU VMM command-buffer replay loss matches
eager base exactly across all steps (max |delta| = 0.000). Compiles clean.
The temporary-disable-collective fix (command_buffer_conversion_pass.cc) is
untouched. ROCm-gated only; no CUDA/BFC changes.

Fix STABLEHLO case and scatter tests with delegate support

- StablehloCaseTest: Pass input tensor type to Build*Subgraph in
  StablehloCaseStaticOpModel and StablehloCaseDynamicOpModel.
  During delegate application (`interpreter->ModifyGraphWithDelegate`),
  any delegate (e.g. YNNPACK, XNNPACK, GPU) queries `IsNodeSupportedByDelegate`
  against all subgraph nodes. Because subgraphs previously defaulted to int32
  tensors, delegates supporting int32 claimed the ops. During `AllocateTensors()`,
  `STABLEHLO_CASE::Prepare()` updated subgraph input types to int16, forcing the
  delegate's `Prepare()` to process int16 tensors which it never inspected or
  accepted during delegate selection.

- StablehloScatter: Use `pre_delegation_execution_plan()` in `GetComputationType()`.
  Higher-order ops (like `stablehlo.scatter`) inspect their body subgraph during
  `Prepare()` to identify the reduction operation. When any delegate claims a
  body subgraph op, TFLite replaces that op in `execution_plan()` with a
  delegate node, causing `STABLEHLO_SCATTER::Prepare()` to fail. Using
  `pre_delegation_execution_plan()` allows `stablehlo.scatter` to inspect the
  original operation regardless of which delegate claimed the body op.

PR #44145: [NVIDIA GPU] Change CollectiveBroadcast op to support dynamic roots

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44145

The current CollectiveBroadcast op hardcodes the root to be the rank 0 in the replica group, this doesn't provide the right level of flexibility. Almost all communication libraries support having dynamic root in the broadcast API. This PR extends the current CB op to take dynamic root determined through an attribute.
1. added an optional "has_dynamic_root" attribute to the CB op
2. once it's set to true, CB op will expect at least 2 operands: the last operand will be a flat array of s32 values which indicate the roots, all other operands will be the inputs. The number of roots should be the same as the number of non-root inputs.
```
  input = f32[128,32]{0,1} parameter(0)
  root = f32[1]{0} parameter(1)
  cb = f32[128,32]{0,1} collective-broadcast(input, root), replica_groups={{1,0},{2,3}}, has_dynamic_root=true
```
This is the PR for the frontend changes including hlo parser and xla builder.

Improve indexing cost model to account for pipelining

The existing Triton indexing performance model frequently underestimated execution times, particularly for skinny GEMMs. This occurred because it was very optimistic with overlapping between compute and memory (assuming perfect overlap). This was particularly off when num_stages = 1.

By integrating DotCostModel that takes software pipelining into account (cl/939776322), this change ensures that memory and compute costs are properly overlapped when pipelining is active and run sequentially otherwise. These improvements ensure the cost model generates more realistic runtime estimates that align with empirical NCU metrics, ultimately leading to better autotuning decisions.

We also added several tests to account for that, all of them were failing before this change.

PR #45219: [SPMD] Fix instruction-height recurrence in schedule-aware collective CSE

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45219

### Problem
`RunOnComputation` in `schedule_aware_collective_ops_cse.cc` computes instruction "height" (distance to root) incorrectly for any multi-user node, corrupting the heuristic that gates schedule-aware CSE.

### Root cause
```cpp
for (auto user : hlo->users()) {
  h = std::max(h, height[user]) + 1;   // +1 applied per user
}
```
The `+ 1` binds outside `std::max`, and `h` is reassigned each iteration, so a node with N users accumulates roughly `+N` instead of a single `+1` on top of the max child height (the result is also order-dependent). For example, two height-0 users yield height 2 where the true longest-path height is 1. This inflated height feeds `coll_height` and `lowest_user_height` into the CSE gate `lowest_user_height(earlier_coll) > coll_height + distance_threshold` (line 152).

### Fix
Move the `+1` inside the max (`std::max(h, height[user] + 1)`) — the canonical longest-path recurrence — matching the no-`+1` reads in `lowest_user_height`.

### Impact / verification
Scheduling/CSE quality heuristic (live-range / peak-memory), not a numerical miscompile. Static reasoning; trivially checkable (two zero-height users → 1, not 2).

[SPMD] Fix instruction-height recurrence in schedule-aware collective CSE

The height recurrence applied `+ 1` to the running max on every user
iteration (`h = std::max(h, height[user]) + 1;`), so a node's height was
inflated by roughly its user count instead of being
max_over_users(height[user]) + 1. That corrupts the height and
lowest_user_height values that gate the CSE schedule-distance heuristic.
Move the +1 inside the max (`std::max(h, height[user] + 1)`), the
canonical longest-path recurrence, matching the no-+1 reads in
lowest_user_height.

Merging this change closes #45219

PR #45220: [HLO] Guard out-of-bounds dimension access in all-gather reshape match

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45220

### Problem
The `get_reshaped_all_gather_dimension` lambda in `GetAllGatherTransformations` (`collective_transformation_reorderer.cc`) can read one past the end of the shape's `DimensionVector`.

### Root cause
The loop (lines 87-93) advances `reshaped_all_gather_dimension` while it is `< rank` **and** `reshaped_num_strides < all_gather_num_strides`. When it exits because the index reached the rank *at the same moment* the stride counts became equal — which happens when the all-gather dimension and any trailing dims are size 1, so `product(dims[all_gather_dim:]) == 1` — the guard at line 94 (`reshaped_num_strides != all_gather_num_strides`) passes, and line 101 then evaluates `shape().dimensions(reshaped_all_gather_dimension)` with the index equal to the rank. `Shape::dimensions(int)` indexes the `DimensionVector` with no bounds check (fires `ABSL_HARDENING_ASSERT` under hardened builds, reads OOB otherwise).

Concrete trigger: all-gather output `[6, 1]`, `all_gather_dimension = 1`, single-user reshape to `[6]`.

### Fix
Return `nullopt` when the index reaches the rank, mirroring the loop's own bound.

### Verification
Static reasoning (loop/index math). No bazel build available on my machine; happy to add a test with a size-1 all-gather dimension followed by a reshape.

PR #45255: [XLA:GPU] Keep VMM mappings alive across executions in command buffer va-remapping run.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45255

## What

Removes the blanket `SynchronizePendingOperations()` drain from `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator::CreateExecutionScope`, so in the command buffer run with va-remapping, deferred deallocations and unmaps from the previous execution stay pending and the next execution reactivates the compatible stale mappings at the same reservation VAs.

## Why

The drain completed every deferred operation before each execution:

* the host spin-waited until the previous execution's teardown seqno retired on the GPU, blocking host run-ahead every step, and
* the reservation-VA mappings were torn down and their physical allocations released, so every step paid fresh physical allocations plus remapping work for each VA-remapped allocation, and the physical handle behind the stable VA changed on every step.

The allocator already handles the leftover state correctly, so the drain is unnecessary:

* `Allocate()` reactivates a compatible stale mapping at the same reservation VA (`TryReuseMappedAllocationAtReservationAddress`, `TryReuseMappedAllocationWithSeparateAddress`), and `Map()` reactivates a stale alias for the same raw allocation and range, keeping the same physical allocation across executions with no unmap/remap work,
* incompatible stale mappings are completed lazily and per-record by the fresh-mapping paths (`EnsureReservationAvailableForFreshMapping` and the `Map()` target preparation), and
* memory pressure is handled by the `ResourceExhausted` reclaim path.

The destructor still synchronizes pending operations so the module-owned VA reservation outlives any stale mappings into it.

With this change, in steady state the VA→physical mapping for VA-remapped allocations is never torn down between executions, which also keeps physical-handle-caching consumers (e.g. `CollectiveMemoryCache` registrations keyed by VA) consistent with the addresses command buffers capture.

## Tests

New tests in `cuda_device_address_vmm_allocator_test.cc`:

* `BackToBackMappedAllocationsReuseMappingsAcrossSteps` — simulates consecutive executable runs over a shared two-slice reservation layout: each step allocates the same slices, runs stream work through the reservation addresses, and defers deallocation at teardown with no synchronization between steps. Asserts later steps reactivate the same physical allocation and verifies stream-ordered data flow through mappings that are never torn down.
* `AllocateIntoReservationRejectsSizeChangeAtSameAddress` — pins that a different-size request at the same reservation offset is rejected as a partial overlap instead of remapping underneath the pending teardown, and that the stale mapping stays reusable for a matching request.

PR #45121: [tsl] Fix FileSystem::Extension for paths with a directory component

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45121

### Problem

`FileSystem::Extension` (`xla/tsl/platform/file_system.cc`) is meant to return the characters after the final `.` in a path's basename. It computes `pos` as the offset of the last `.` **within `basename`**, but then constructs the returned `string_view` from the **full `path`**:

```cpp
absl::string_view basename = this->Basename(path);
size_t pos = basename.rfind('.');
...
return absl::string_view(path.data() + pos + 1, path.size() - (pos + 1));  // uses path, not basename
```

`basename` is a later substring of `path` whenever `path` has a directory component, so applying the basename-relative `pos` to `path` indexes into the wrong location:

```
Extension("dir/file.txt")      -> "ile.txt"    (expected "txt")
Extension("a/b/c/name.tar.gz") -> "e.tar.gz"   (expected "gz")
Extension("/tmp/foo.log")      -> "/foo.log"   (expected "log")
Extension("file.txt")          -> "txt"        (correct — no directory)
Extension("noext")             -> ""           (correct)
```

The result is correct only in the `basename == path` case (no directory component).

### Fix

Build the returned view from `basename`, which is where `pos` was computed:

```cpp
return absl::string_view(basename.data() + pos + 1,
                         basename.size() - (pos + 1));
```

### Tests

Added `RamFileSystemTest.ExtensionUsesBasenameForPathsWithDirectory` to `xla/tsl/platform/ram_file_system_test.cc` (using `RamFileSystem` to exercise the inherited `FileSystem::Extension`). It covers directory-prefixed paths, an absolute path, a no-directory path, and a no-extension path; it fails on the current code and passes with the fix. There was previously no test covering `FileSystem::Extension`, which is how this survived.

PR #44295: [XLA:GPU] Achieve command buffer persisitent address through DeviceAddressVmmAllocator va-remapping APIs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44295

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the command-buffer VMM allocation step in the stack:

Previous PR: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44355
Next PR: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44296

This change routes command-buffer execution allocation through `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` using `se::DeviceAddressVmmAllocator`:

- Creates executable/executor-scoped VMM remapping state for command-buffer allocation indexes.
- Reserves a stable virtual address range and assigns deterministic offsets for command-buffer-visible allocations.
- Allocates command-buffer temp/live-out buffers through the VMM allocator when VA remapping is active.
- Maps entry-parameter buffers into reservation-backed aliases for command-buffer execution, then unmaps those aliases after execution.
- Synchronizes pending VMM operations when the executable-scoped allocator is destroyed.
- Keeps returned-output/live-out policy inside `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` so returned buffers expose the expected physical allocation address instead of a reservation alias.
- Moves command-buffer update-mode/index collection and returned-output allocation-index collection into `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator`, keeping `GpuExecutable` and PJRT call sites focused on scope creation, allocation generation, execution, and teardown.
- Leaves PJRT teardown behavior and existing `buffer_allocations` naming unchanged.

🎯 Justification
Command-buffer replay is sensitive to device address changes. VMM reservations let XLA present stable virtual addresses for buffers captured by command buffers while still allowing the physical backing allocations, including parameter buffers, to vary between executions.

Centralizing this policy in `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` keeps the VMM reservation, remapping, returned-output handling, and command-buffer allocation-index collection in one owner. That makes the `GpuExecutable` and PJRT execution paths smaller and prepares the follow-up command-buffer update-info runtime change in #44296.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
⚡️ Performance Improvement, ♻️ Cleanup

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Not run locally. This PR adds the runtime allocation/remapping plumbing expected to reduce command-buffer update overhead for VMM-capable command-buffer executions, especially with `xla_gpu_command_buffer_update_mode=NEVER_UPDATE` or `CAPTURE_CMD_NEVER_UPDATE`.

🧪 Unit Tests:
No new unit tests were added in this PR. Existing focused coverage was run:

`bazel test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_test`

🧪 Execution Tests:

PR #44296: [XLA:GPU] A generic XLA runtime to support stable allocation addresses for command buffer.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44296

📝 Summary of Changes
Add allocation address policy plumbing for GPU command-buffer execution on top of #44295.

Core idea: `AllocationAddressInfo` is the small runtime contract that tells command-buffer code which buffer allocation addresses are stable for the current execution.

The flow works as follows:
- `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` builds the execution `BufferAllocations` and decides which allocation indices have persistent command-buffer-visible addresses. This can include global constants, VMM reservation-backed allocations, and any other allocation whose visible address is stable for the execution.
- `GpuExecutable` passes that information to thunks as `AllocationAddressInfo`. The `address_info_ready` flag tells consumers whether this policy is finalized; before it is ready, command-buffer code keeps the conservative update behavior.
- Once `address_info_ready` is true, `persistent_alloc_indices` is the source of truth for stable allocation addresses. Any allocation index not listed there is treated as dynamic by command-buffer consumers.
- `CommandBufferThunk` uses this policy to limit address-change checks to dynamic allocations when deciding whether a command buffer needs recording or updating.
- `CommandExecutor` uses the same policy at command granularity: if every allocation referenced by a command is persistent, that command can skip update recording because its command-buffer-visible addresses are stable.

This gives the runtime a generic way to expose persistent addresses to command-buffer execution without tying the command-buffer update logic to one specific stabilization mechanism.

This PR:
- Adds `Thunk::AllocationAddressInfo` as the runtime contract for allocation address stability.
- Threads optional allocation address info through `GpuExecutable`, PJRT GPU execution, thunk initialization, and thunk execution.
- Computes persistent allocation indices in `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator`, including global constant buffer allocations.
- Treats allocations outside `persistent_alloc_indices` as dynamically allocated for command-buffer update decisions.
- Updates `CommandBufferThunk` to check only dynamic allocation addresses when deciding whether a command buffer needs recording or updating.
- Updates `CommandExecutor` to skip command updates when every allocation referenced by a command is persistent.
- Caches command-buffer dynamic-allocation checks once the address info is ready.
- Adds and updates unit coverage for allocation-address policy behavior and allocation-index filtering.

🎯 Justification
#44295 moves command-buffer VA remapping into VMM-backed execution `BufferAllocations`, giving some command-buffer-visible addresses that can stay stable across executions.

This PR generalizes that stability into allocation address information. Commands that only reference persistent allocations do not need command-buffer updates just because underlying physical allocations changed. Commands that reference any non-persistent allocation still go through the existing dynamic-address update checks.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
✨ New Feature, ♻️ Cleanup, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A. This PR introduces runtime address-policy plumbing and cleanup; it does not claim a measured performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:
Validated locally with:
- `bazel test --test_output=errors //xla/backends/gpu/runtime:command_buffer_thunk_test`
- `bazel test --test_output=errors //xla/backends/gpu/runtime:dynamic_slice_fusion_v2_thunk_test`
- `bazel test --test_output=errors --test_filter='CommandBufferThunkTest.UpdatePolicyIgnoresVaRemappedAllocations|GpuExecutableTest.CommandBufferAllocationIndexesIncludeMlirConstants' //xla/backends/gpu/runtime:command_buffer_thunk_test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_test`

Additional validation:
- `bazel build --config=clang-tidy-noerrors //xla:debug_options_flags_test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_buffer_allocator //xla/pjrt/gpu:se_gpu_pjrt_client`

PR #45164: [XLA:GPU] Cache CommandExecutor update requirements

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45164

📝 Summary of Changes

Precompute `CommandExecutor::requires_update_on_initialize()` and
`CommandExecutor::requires_update_on_execute()` during the constructor's
existing recursive command walk. Subsequent queries return the cached values
instead of walking all top-level and nested commands again.

🎯 Justification

`CommandBufferThunk` queries these properties while initializing and executing
command buffers. Their results are invariant after command executor
construction, so recursively walking the command tree and making virtual calls
for every query is unnecessary. This cleanup reduces host overhead for command
buffers, particularly those with large nested while or conditional bodies.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

claim an end-to-end performance improvement.

[XLA:GPU] Add a `xtile-scalarize-scan` pass

`xtile.scan` will be emitted for XLA `kScan` HLO ops. The scan dimension and combiner region will be emitted verbatim, which is a) operating on input slices and b) not yet tiled.

This change addresses a)

PR #45077: [XLA:GPU][ROCm] Fix ScaledDotRewriter retaining sub-byte element size on fp4 upcast

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45077

When ScaledDotRewriter upcasts an fp4 (F4E2M1FN) operand to BF16, the Convert helper copied the operand shape and only changed the element type, keeping the source's custom element_size_in_bits=4. This produced an illegal bf16[...]{:E(4)} shape that CpuGpuShapeVerifier rejects with "does not support custom element sizes on non-sub-byte types".

Use ShapeUtil::ChangeElementType, which clears the custom element size for non-sub-byte targets. Surfaced on gfx1250 for mixed fp4xfp8 scaled dots, where the fissioned rewrite is the sole autotuning candidate and gets verified; latent on gfx950 where native hipBLASLt wins autotuning.

PR #45093: [XLA:GPU][ROCm] Fix absl::bit_cast in device code for GCC 13 compatibility

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45093

PR #44389 introduced `buffer_debug_float_check_kernel_rocm.cu.cc`, which uses `absl::bit_cast` in `__device__ constexpr` initializers. This breaks the rocm_clang_local build on Ubuntu 24.04 where GCC 13 is the default.

GCC 13 reimplemented `std::__or_<>` using __or_fn helper functions that are not annotated `__host__ __device__`. This causes clang/HIP to reject instantiation of `std::is_trivially_copyable` (via `__is_complete_or_unbounded`) from device context during overload resolution, even when the type is complete and the slow overload is never actually called.

absl::bit_cast triggers this via its static_assert on is_trivially_copyable. Replace `absl::bit_cast` with `__builtin_bit_cast` in `__device__ code`, which is a compiler intrinsic and bypasses standard library type trait machinery entirely. Also substitute the bfloat16 infinity bit pattern (0x7F80) directly.

PR #44983: [XLA:GPU] Reuse stale VMM mappings in mapped Allocate in DeviceAddressVmmAllocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44983

📝 Summary of Changes

This upstream follow-up carries the behavior change from [shawnwang18/xla#3](https://github.com/shawnwang18/xla/pull/3) after the prerequisite helper and `Map()` work from openxla/xla#44861 landed on `main`.

It updates mapped `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Allocate(..., MemoryReservation*, ...)` to reuse compatible stale VMM mappings:

- Reactivates a matching stale allocator record when `return_reservation_address=true`.
- Reactivates the allocator-owned returned VA and caller reservation alias together when `return_reservation_address=false`.
- Waits for an undersized or otherwise incompatible stale allocation to finish deferred teardown before falling back to a fresh allocation.
- Rejects partial overlaps with active or stale allocator/reservation ranges, completes exact stale overlaps, and reports active overlaps as duplicate ownership.
- Uses the shared `TryWithPendingReclaim()` retry policy so PA-budget pressure reclaims completed pending frees before waiting for stream work.

🎯 Justification

This reduces VMM teardown/remap churn and avoidable host-side waits for command-buffer-style GPU workloads that repeatedly allocate the same reservation-backed virtual address ranges. Keeping this behavior layer separate from the already-landed helper and `Map()` changes narrows review to mapped-allocation ownership, reuse eligibility, and fallback behavior.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement, ♻️ Cleanup

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

No benchmark results were collected for this split.

Expected benefit: fewer VMM unmap/remap operations and fewer blocking waits when mapped allocation requests can reuse stale allocator or reservation mappings.

🧪 Unit Tests:

Added two focused cases to the existing CUDA VMM allocator test:

- `AllocateIntoReservationReusesPendingReservationAddress` verifies stale
  allocation reuse when the reservation address is returned.
- `AllocateIntoReservationReusesPendingAllocatorAndReservationAddresses`
  verifies paired reactivation of the allocator-owned address and caller
  reservation alias.

Validation on this rebased branch:

```bash
clang-format --dry-run --Werror xla/stream_executor/device_address_vmm_allocator.cc
clang-format --dry-run --Werror xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_device_address_vmm_allocator_test.cc
bazel build //xla/stream_executor:device_address_vmm_allocator
bazel test --config=cuda_nvcc \
  --repo_env=HERMETIC_CUDA_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES=sm_90 \
  --cache_test_results=no --test_output=errors \
  //xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_device_address_vmm_allocator_test
```

Result: formatting and build checks passed; all 28 CUDA allocator tests passed
on an NVIDIA H200.

🧪 Execution Tests:

No separate workload-level execution tests were added. The full CUDA allocator
test target above executed on GPU with 28 tests passing.

PR #45000: [XLA:GPU] Fix device association for reordered GPU communicator splits

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45000

📝 Summary of Changes

Fix GPU clique splitting when a child clique reorders the parent ranks. XLA now emits each parent communicator, split key, and device/executor together in child-rank order. Add a two-GPU regression for `[D0, D1] → [D1, D0]`.

🎯 Justification

The old code built parallel arrays in different orders, which could pair an NCCL communicator with the wrong GPU `StreamExecutor`. Wrong-device memory registration could make ranks use inconsistent NCCL paths and hang collectives. This fix preserves the communicator/device association.

### Example

For parent clique `[D0, D1]` and reordered child clique `[D1, D0]`, the old code built:

```text
parent communicator: [D0, D1]
split key:           [ 1,  0]
executor:            [D1, D0]
```

The arrays are consumed by index, so the D0 communicator was paired with the D1 executor, and the D1 communicator with the D0 executor. The communicator split could succeed, but later buffer registration used the wrong physical GPU.

The fix builds all fields in child-rank order:

```text
parent communicator: [D1, D0]
split key:           [ 0,  1]
executor:            [D1, D0]
```

Each communicator now remains paired with its matching device and executor.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable; this is a correctness fix.

🧪 Unit Tests:

- PASS: `bazel test //xla/backends/gpu/collectives:gpu_cliques_test --test_filter=GpuCliquesTest.SplitCliquesKeepsReorderedRanksOnCorrectExecutors`
- PASS: `bazel test //xla/backends/gpu/collectives:gpu_cliques_test --test_filter=GpuCliquesTest.Split*`

🧪 Execution Tests:

The two-GPU Loopback regression exercises reordered clique splitting. The original four-GPU Muon reproducer also completed one training step with source-built NCCL 2.30.7.

commit.message:
Fix flexbuffers vector creation bug in MLIR TFLite export

---

When exporting StableHLOComposite attributes, flexbuffers::Builder was being called with the attribute name as a key for every vector element. In flexbuffers, passing a key to a Vector element pushes both the key and the value to the stack, causing the vector to be parsed with twice its intended length (with the key interleaved).

This change removes the key from the vector element calls, and only uses the key when starting the parent vector, which matches the flexbuffers::Builder API expectation for Vectors.

- Also fixed a typo where `isa<StringAttr>(attr)` was checking the Array attribute instead of the element.

- Updated test to pass actual vector values for serialization

- If axes is a numpy array, call .tolist() directly

[XLA:GPU] Back up read-write buffers in device memory for float checker

Improve efficiency of the float checker crash dump mode by storing buffer backups in device memory instead of host memory. This avoids expensive device-to-host copies (over PCIe) during normal execution.

To minimize memory overhead, a single global scratch buffer is allocated statically and shared sequentially among all instrumented thunks. This reduces the peak memory footprint of the backups from cumulative to the maximum required by any single thunk.

1. The global backup buffer is allocated statically during the thunk wrapping pass.
2. Slices of this buffer are assigned to each thunk's backup operations, with alignment preserved.
3. Device-to-host copies are only performed when a numerical anomaly is actually detected, keeping the slow transfer strictly in the cold path.
