PR #44885: [XLA:GPU] Track XTile scaled-dot element types

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44885

📝 Summary of Changes
Make xtile.dot_scaled carry logical LHS/RHS element types explicitly, instead of deriving them from operand tensor element types during Triton lowering. This lets XTile represent packed FP4 scaled-dot operands correctly: the operand tensor can use physical i8 storage, while the dot semantics remain f4E2M1FN. This is the first PR in the decomposition of larger scaled-dot fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44223.

🎯 Justification
XTile cannot defer FP4 packing until Triton lowering because packing changes the storage value, not just the final `tt.dot_scaled` attributes. For `f4E2M1FN`, two logical elements are stored in one byte, so the packed dimension (minor vs major), tile offsets, and load/result value type all need to be computed in the tiled XTile emission path before `xtile.dot_scaled` is lowered. A logical `tensor<128x64xf4E2M1FN>` tile and a physical `tensor<128x32xi8>` tile are different IR values with different indexing contracts. Converting only at Triton lowering would require rewriting producers (i.e. transpose in front of scaled dot after canonicalization), shapes, offsets, and layout decisions after the fact.

This matches Triton boundary: XTile models the actual packed storage tile, and Triton lowering still has the semantic type information needed to emit `tt.dot_scaled lhs = e2m1 rhs = e2m1`.

[XLA:GPU] Fix XLA LRN mixed precision error for float16 and bfloat16 inputs

When tf.raw_ops.LRN or LRNGrad is compiled with XLA for float16 or bfloat16 inputs, compilation fails with an internal error due to mixed precision operands in binary operations (e.g. multiply). This happens because attribute scalar constants (bias_, alpha_, beta_) were created using xla::ConstantR0<float>, which hardcodes F32 precision.

This change replaces xla::ConstantR0<float> with XlaHelpers::FloatLiteral(builder, input_type(0), ...) in LRNOp::Compile and LRNGradOp::Compile so that scalar attribute constants match the precision of the input tensor.

PR #43894: [GPU] Add PDL launch insertion.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/43894

📝 Summary of Changes
Inserts `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` instructions between Triton GEMM mainloops and epilogues. They enable further overlaps of kernels on top of the existing base implementation (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/38544). The insertion logic is based on the observation that most Triton GEMMs, even those without epilogue in HLO, do have epilogues at lower levels - moving / transposing output data through shared memory. This creates an opportunity to increase productive overlaps with subsequent kernels.

Using launch_dependents instructions requires disabling non-coherent / invariant loads for dependent data in successors being launched as these can not be guarded by their PDL waits.

🎯 Justification
Speeds up (typically inference) benchmarks by overlapping independent phases of kernels.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 939804756

Calculate `GpuProfiler::GetScratchBytes` using BufferUses in Autotuner

- Old logic: Scans physical `BufferAllocation`s and only counts those where `IsPreallocatedTempBuffer()` is true. This misses scratch buffers that the compiler overlays onto live-out (output) allocations to save memory.

- New logic: Walks the executed `Thunk` sequence and sums the sizes of all logical `BufferUse::Scratch` slices, accurately capturing scratch usage regardless of physical overlay optimizations.

Example (32MB matmul scratch overlaid on a 157MB live-out output buffer):
- Old logic: Returns 0 bytes (skips the live-out allocation).
- New logic: Returns 32MB (correctly extracts the scratch thunk use).

Also had to a const way to Walk Thunks

#### Why this is needed

The current logic relies on the `BufferAssignments` being alive, since the `buffer` variable which holds an `HloValue` is owned by the `BufferAssignments` brass.

I'm in the process of removing the `BufferAssignment` from the executable since it it cannot be re-created when loading an AOT binary, and its not really needed. So we need to get rid of this implicit dependency before doing so.

PR #44861: [XLA:GPU]  Reuse stale VMM reservation mappings in Map in DeviceAddressVmmAllocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44861

📝 Summary of Changes

This PR adds the common helper layer for stale VMM mapping reuse:

- range-overlap helpers for `DeviceAddressBase` virtual address intervals;
- `FindOverlappingRecord()` for active/stale allocator and reservation records;
- helpers to remove a pending deallocation entry by kind/address;
- helpers to reactivate stale reservation records;
- helpers to wait for and complete one selected stale allocator or reservation overlap;
- documentation updates for full-range reservation ownership and stale record reuse;
- `GetRawAllocation()` keeps returning raw allocations for stale allocator addresses until deferred teardown drains.

It also wires the reservation reuse path into `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Map()`:

- finds a reusable stale reservation record for exact full-range remaps;
- rejects unsupported partial stale reservation overlap with an internal error;
- waits for a selected pending stale reservation when the overlap cannot be reused;
- reactivates a stale reservation record instead of allocating a fresh mapping record when reuse is valid.

Mapped `Allocate()` reuse is still left for the next stacked PR.

Stack:
1. openxla/xla#44861: helper/docs foundation plus stale reservation reuse in `Map()`. This PR.
2. shawnwang18/xla#3: reuse stale mappings in mapped `Allocate()`.

Note: the original upstream draft PR #44174 is unchanged. The former fork PR shawnwang18/xla#2 has been merged into this PR branch.

🎯 Justification
The original PR touched several allocator paths at once. This updated split now gives reviewers the shared bookkeeping primitives together with the first direct caller, so the lifetime invariants can be reviewed in context before the mapped `Allocate()` path is added.

This is important for VMM allocator reuse because remapping a full stale reservation can avoid unnecessary reservation bookkeeping churn while still preserving correctness for partial overlaps and pending deferred teardown.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
⚡️ Performance Improvement, ♻️ Cleanup

Raise no-data proto allocation cap from 64 MB to 2 GB

kMaxBytesFromProtoNoData bounds the zero-fill path (in_n == 0). The 64 MB cap rejected legitimately default-initialized large tensors: a 2 GB bool variable set to False serializes with an empty value list (in_n == 0), so the no-data guard tripped. 2 GB is the ceiling on a single serialized protobuf message, so it still bounds amplification from tiny no-data messages while allowing large default-init. Fixes the saver_large_variable_test regression reported on the PR.

commit.message:
fix math_ops: promote to complex128 in sign() to avoid both kernel mismatch and FTZ underflow (PR review feedback)

Addresses @dmiltr3's review comments on PR #117023:

1. Kernel signature mismatch: The ComplexAbs C++ kernel rejects
   mismatched input/output precision (complex64 -> float64 throws
   InvalidArgumentError). The previous attempt to force Tout=float64
   on a complex64 input was broken at runtime.

2. Division underflow on FTZ systems: Even if the magnitude is
   computed in float64, the vectorized complex division uses an
   intermediate conjugate product on the original input precision,
   which underflows to 0 on Flush-To-Zero systems when |z| is below
   the input dtype's smallest normal value.

Fix: promote the input itself to complex128 for the entire
computation. Both |z| and the division now happen in double precision
(underflow threshold ~1e-154 vs ~1e-19 for float32). The kernel
signatures match cleanly (complex128 -> float64 is supported), and
the final result is cast back to the original input dtype.

Also adds a regression test verifying sign() of subnormal-magnitude
complex64 values returns the correct unit-magnitude result.

Fixes tf#116945.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 938812415

This change introduces a new sweep-line buffer assignment algorithm for AssignBuffersForComputations, similar to go/xla-fast-buffer-assignment. It adds `FAST_MERGE` to `AssignmentAlgorithmForComputationsWithoutOrderingProto` and implements `FastMergeBufferAllocationsManagerForComputationsWithoutOrdering` to track buffer liveness and reuse expired allocations from a free pool.

Instead of the default O(N * M) naive allocation scan (where N is the number of buffers and M is the number of allocations, leading to O(N^2) worst-case), this algorithm achieves O(N log M) time complexity for allocation reuse.

Key features:

1. Incoming buffers are processed in increasing order of their live range start times (BufferOrder::kLiveRangeStart). It tracks active allocations in a min-heap (`active_allocations_`) ordered by their maximum live range end time.

2. Before assigning a new buffer, it advances the sweep-line (`UpdateLiveness`), moving any active allocations that have fully expired (max_end_time <= new_buffer.min_start) into a free pool. By this, allocations in the free pool are guaranteed to have no live range conflicts with the incoming buffer.

3. The free pool (`free_pool_`) indexes available allocations by color and size using balanced trees (absl::btree_multimap). Finding the smallest fitting reusable allocation takes O(log M) time via `lower_bound`, avoiding linear scans over all existing allocations.

commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Prune inactive operands in EmitConcatenate.

In EmitConcatenate, if some operands are statically inactive (tile size 0), they are lowered to unit tensors of shape 1x1x1x1. This causes type mismatch in the generated scf.if when compared to active operands which have the correct tiled shape.

PR #44224: [XLA:GPU] Migrate VMM allocator bookkeeping to AllocationRecord

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44224

📝 Summary of Changes
Ports DeviceAddressVmmAllocator bookkeeping to AllocationRecord for both allocator addresses and reservation aliases.

This change moves Allocate(), mapped Allocate(), Deallocate(), Map(), UnMap(), pending allocator deallocation, pending reservation unmap, reuse, and allocator/reservation lookup state onto AllocationRecord-backed bookkeeping. The old ReservationMapping maps are replaced with active/stale reservation-record indexes, and pending entries now carry enough record identity to complete or reuse stale allocator and reservation mappings safely.

🎯 Justification
This completes the VMM allocator bookkeeping migration in one reviewable PR. Keeping allocator-address and reservation-address lifetime in one record makes ownership, stale-state transitions, deferred teardown, and reuse behavior easier to reason about than split map-based state.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
♻️ Cleanup

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:
No new unit test target was added; this is a refactor of existing VMM allocator bookkeeping.

Propagate debug information to fusion search space.

Previously, we were cloning the HloModule without the debug options and then using the debug options in the cloned module to check if experimental tiling was enabled. Because the default is false, the tests were never testing this pathway.

The tests were previously depending on pads to be "possible in triton", but not possible to get tiled. PR #37766: fix: add recursion depth limit to HLO parser

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/37766

📝 Summary of Changes

Add recursion depth tracking to HLO parser to prevent stack overflow crashes from deeply nested input. A shared `current_recursion_depth_` counter is added to 6 recursive parse functions. When the configurable limit (default 500) is exceeded, the parser returns a graceful `"maximum recursion depth exceeded"` error instead of crashing.

🎯 Justification

The HLO parser is vulnerable to stack exhaustion from maliciously crafted or malformed deeply nested HLO text. This is reachable anywhere HLO text is accepted (tools, file loading, etc.).

Note the parser is not recommended for production use and can be considered as a debug API. This issue was disclosed & discussed with the maintainers.

Fixes OSS-Fuzz [#390461336](https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/390461336) from Tensorflow.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A -- not a performance change. The added overhead is essentially one integer increment/compare and a trivial RAII guard per recursive parse call.

🧪 Unit Tests:

Five new tests for the HLO parser:

- `DeeplyNestedOperandsExceedsRecursionLimit`: verifies `add(add(add...` nesting triggers the depth error at a reduced limit of 10.
- `DeeplyNestedShapesExceedsRecursionLimit`: verifies `(((f32[])))` shape nesting triggers the depth error.
- `DeeplyNestedTupleLiteralsExceedsRecursionLimit`: verifies `(((0)))` tuple literal nesting triggers the depth error.
- `DeeplyNestedInlineComputationsExceedsRecursionLimit`: verifies nested `call(...), to_apply={...}` inline computations trigger the depth error.
- `DeeplyNestedOperandsDoesNotStackOverflow`: regression test with 50,000 nesting levels using the default limit, confirming no stack overflow crash.
- `DeeplyNestedUntypedTupleLiteralExceedsRecursionLimit`: verifies that deeply nested untyped tuple literals in `literal=` attributes hit the recursion limit instead of overflowing the stack.

Test output:

Redact google strings from --json output for parity with text report

The text report filters lines containing google (grep -v -i google) to
avoid leaking internal hostnames, depot paths, or build configurations
when users upload diagnostic logs. The new --json path wrote raw env
vars (TPU_NAME, XLA_FLAGS, paths) and TF device/version strings straight
to tf_env.json without that filter.

Add a recursive redact() helper that replaces any string value containing
google (case-insensitive) with [redacted] and apply it to the report
before writing, so tf_env.json matches the redaction safety of tf_env.txt.

Addresses review feedback from @sgarciagoogle.

[XLA:GPU] emit reshape as reshape + broadcast

That creates correct IR for cases when reshape introduces trivial dimensions that in have tile size > 1.
Previously that lead to an errors such as `Reshape input and output shapes must be the same, got 1x1x2x16 -> 1x2x1x2x16x1` as we blindly assume\d that if input and output shapes are compatible then tiles must be as well.

That also required to fix broadcast lowering for cases when we "broadcast" to scalar - but that keeps the emitter logic much simpler.

[StableHLO] Fix 2 bugs related to `interpreter.print` inside `interpreter.run_parallel`

We fix the following 2 bugs:-

1. When an `interpreter.print` op was used inside a function called by `interpreter.run_parallel`, the interpreter was failing with `LLVM ERROR: Unsupported op: interpreter.print`. This error was thrown in the `eval()` function because the `DefaultInterpreterFallback` wasn't passed into it when it was called inside `evalRunParallelOp()`. The `eval()` function doesn't handle `interpreter` ops without the presence of the right fallback. We fix that.
2. After this was fixed and the `interpreter.print` op was getting recognized, another issue surfaced which was that the parallel runs were making the printing interleaved and illegible. We fix that by using a lock in the `interpreter.print` op.

PR #44763: [XLA:GPU][ROCm] Fix rocm_clang_local host toolchain under Bazel 8

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44763

Under Bazel 8, rocm_clang_local's host and target C++ compiles fall back to the autodetected gcc, which rejects the Clang-only warning flags from --config=warnings (-Wself-assign, -Wthread-safety-analysis, etc.).

Register the ROCm crosstool via --extra_toolchains so toolchain resolution routes C++ compiles through the ROCm wrapper (clang via CLANG_COMPILER_PATH) while -x rocm still goes to hipcc. Drop the --crosstool_top, which is a no-op now.

PR #44726: [XLA:GPU] ROCm VMM enablement: wire DeviceAddressVmmAllocator into PJRT GPU client

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44726

## Summary
Final integration step for the ROCm VMM allocator stack (the allocator layers + factory + tests landed via #43947). This wires the allocator into the runtime so it is actually selectable end-to-end:

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc`: add a ROCm branch to the `kVmm` allocator selection so `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` constructs `RocmDeviceAddressVmmAllocator` on ROCm. The `GOOGLE_CUDA` path is left byte-for-byte unchanged; ROCm support is added purely under `TENSORFLOW_USE_ROCM` / `if_rocm`, so the CUDA build is unaffected.
- `xla/pjrt/gpu/BUILD`: add the `rocm_device_address_vmm_allocator` dependency under `if_rocm`.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test.cc`: extend the existing CUDA `VmmTest` (`VmmAllocatorCanBeSet`) to also run on ROCm, asserting the client's allocator is a `RocmDeviceAddressVmmAllocator`.

Small, self-contained change (~38 lines) on top of `main` now that the allocator stack has merged.

## Test plan
- [ ] `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test` `VmmTest.VmmAllocatorCanBeSet` passes on a ROCm (gfx942/gfx950) device.
- [ ] Build `//xla/pjrt/gpu:se_gpu_pjrt_client` under `--config=rocm`.
- [ ] Manual: `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` selects the ROCm VMM allocator.

[XLA:GPU] Optimize HLO instruction lookup in float check pass

Avoid O(N^2) compilation slowdown by building a map of HLO instructions once per pass and using it for O(1) lookups when wrapping thunks.

Originally, the pass performed an O(N) search for every thunk, resulting in quadratic complexity. The O(N) search helper is retained but restricted to the anomaly reporting path, which is a cold path and does not affect compilation time.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 937375485

Fix NaN propagation in CPU segment reduction ops and document CPU-GPU discrepancy

CPU segment reductions (SegmentMin, SegmentMax, UnsortedSegmentMin,
UnsortedSegmentMax) now propagate NaN values by using Eigen's
PropagateNaN policy via template aliases MinReducerPropagateNaN and
MaxReducerPropagateNaN.

GPU segment reductions retain their existing behavior (NaNs are not
propagated) due to hardware/atomic operation constraints with
GpuAtomicMin/GpuAtomicMax. This CPU-GPU discrepancy is documented in
comments and tests.

Changes:
- segment_reduction_ops_impl_1.cc: Use MinReducerPropagateNaN/
  MaxReducerPropagateNaN aliases for SegmentMin/SegmentMax (int32 index)
- segment_reduction_ops_impl_2.cc: Same for int64 index path
- segment_reduction_ops_impl.h: Add NaN propagation to MinOp/MaxOp
  for UnsortedSegmentMin/UnsortedSegmentMax (CPU path)
- segment_reduction_ops.h: Document CPU-GPU NaN discrepancy
- segment_reduction_ops_test.py: Add testNaNPropagation for both
  sorted and unsorted segment reductions, with correct CPU vs GPU
  assertions

2b0faa079990366b483757dffb23cd58526dbfd6 by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Restore main Bazel deps for Bazel 8 migration

The old migration branch carried older Bzlmod pins for curl, gutil, pybind11_bazel, re2, xxd, and zlib. Those downgrades are not part of the Bazel 8.7.0 migration and caused the JAX Bzlmod job to fail while linking libcurl because the older curl package did not provide the expected version script.

Keep the dependency versions from main, and update the WORKSPACE rules_cc archive to 0.2.17 as well. rules_cc 0.2.17 requires its compatibility proxy repository in WORKSPACE mode, so initialize that proxy after bazel_features_deps() and before the ML toolchain setup loads rules_cc internals.

The ROCm CI job still compiles some actions with GCC while the global warnings config includes Clang-only positive warning flags. Filter those unsupported flags only for rocm_base using --nocopt so the ROCm build is not broken by compiler-specific warnings.

--
d013e4a10a63f910f81318c71a246c9df83e52a8 by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Fix workspace rules_cc and ROCm warnings

The previous change tried to align the WORKSPACE rules_cc archive with the Bzlmod rules_cc version from main. That does not work for JAX jobs that build JAX with --override_repository=xla because JAX's WORKSPACE does not initialize the cc_compatibility_proxy repository required by newer rules_cc releases. Keep the Bzlmod rules_cc pin at 0.2.17, but use the old migration's workspace-only rules_cc 0.2.0 archive so WORKSPACE consumers do not need the new proxy repository.

The ROCm job also failed before analysis because Bazel 8 rejects --nocopt as an rc-file option here. Remove that attempted rocm_base filter and instead drop the exact Clang-only positive warning flags from warnings.bazelrc that GCC rejected in the ROCm build. The rest of the warnings config, including -Werror and the broadly supported warning flags, stays enabled.

--
c4afc3dba94cafc207810fd6ddd894675d7e4f59 by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Remove C-only warning suppressions from shared warnings

The ROCm XLA job uses GCC for some C++ compilations while the shared warnings config applies -Werror globally. GCC reports -Wno-strict-prototypes and -Wno-pointer-sign as C/ObjC-only options when compiling C++, and those diagnostics become hard errors under -Werror.

Remove those two suppressions from warnings.bazelrc so the Bazel 8 ROCm build can compile C++ actions with GCC. The rest of the warnings config remains enabled.

--
f5b95abcfa8515a3b1637d50f080964484b5a6cf by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Scope GCC warning downgrade to ROCm

ROCm still failed after removing the first two C-only suppressions because GCC also reports C++-only warning options on C sources under the global warnings config. Removing every language-specific suppression globally would weaken the default warnings config too broadly.

Keep the warnings config intact except for the positive Clang-only warning flags that GCC treats as invalid options, and add -Wno-error only under rocm_base. That lets the ROCm GCC path tolerate language-specific warning-option diagnostics while preserving -Werror for the normal warning configuration.

--
16b6cd9de31904ecb783750609bb148343e2c028 by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Respect ROCm clang toolchain selection

ROCm CI selects rocm_clang_official, which passes CLANG_COMPILER_PATH as an action environment variable and uses clang_local for the C++ toolchain. After the Bazel 8 migration moved local C++ autoconfiguration through rules_cc, CI still fell back to /usr/bin/gcc for host/link actions, which surfaced as GCC warning handling and linker failures.

Restore the warning configuration to match main and remove the broad ROCm -Wno-error workaround. Pass CLANG_COMPILER_PATH, CC, and BAZEL_COMPILER as repository environment for the ROCm clang config so both rocm_configure and rules_cc C++ autoconfiguration see the intended Clang compiler during repository setup.

--
c78d750fc95999a89d6b02d891fdd591fe9a425a by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Configure ROCm clang path for repository setup

ROCm CI uses rocm_clang_official and rocm_configure reads CLANG_COMPILER_PATH from repository environment when generating the ROCm crosstool wrapper. Passing it only as action_env leaves repository setup without the explicit Clang path under the Bazel 8/rules_cc migration.

Keep the Clang path in repo_env so the ROCm crosstool is generated with the intended host compiler, but do not override global CC or BAZEL_COMPILER. Those broader overrides bypassed the ROCm wrapper for -x rocm actions and caused raw clang to reject the ROCm pseudo-language.

--
fec3545c9974fcf80c1c641296bb08cfe830ed75 by Corentin Kerisit <corentin.kerisit@gmail.com>:

Expose ROCm sysdeps headers

ROCm's rocm_smi headers include libdrm/drm.h, which is shipped in the hermetic ROCm distribution under lib/rocm_sysdeps/include. The generated local_config_rocm repository only exposed the top-level ROCm include tree, so hermetic ROCm builds could see rocm_smi/kfd_ioctl.h but not the libdrm headers it includes.

Add a dedicated rocm_sysdeps_includes target and depend on it from rocm_headers_includes so Bazel propagates a virtual include root for the bundled sysdeps headers. This keeps the build independent of libdrm-dev being installed on the CI image or present in the hermetic C++ sysroot.

[XLA] Fix non-array handling in `xla::ShapeUtil::MakeValidatedShape()`

`xla::Shape::mutable_layout()` cannot be called for non-array `xla::Shape`, even if we are not going to mutate the layout. Since non-array types are dimension-less in XLA, we enforce this invariant within `xla::ShapeUtil::MakeValidatedShape()` and skip accessing `xla::Shape::mutable_layout()` there.

Ultimately, this fix makes it safe to call `xla::ShapeUtil::MakeValidatedShape()` from PJRT C API `xla::GetOutputShapeHelper()`, which may use `xla::ShapeUtil::MakeValidatedShape()` for a token type shape after https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44400.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 936787328

Validate the index in TensorListSetItem to prevent a segfault

TensorListSetItem read the index as int32 and used it without validating
it. An out-of-range int32 index (e.g. INT64_MAX truncated to int32, which
wraps to -1) passed the unsigned `index >= size()` check via integer
promotion and then indexed `tensors()[index]` out of bounds, causing a
segmentation fault even with resize_if_index_out_of_bounds=True.

Reject negative indices with InvalidArgument, and reject indices that
would grow a bounded list past max_num_elements (mirroring the existing
check in TensorListPushBack), which also avoids unbounded allocation for
very large indices. Cast to size_t before adding 1 in the resize path to
avoid signed overflow when index is INT32_MAX.

Adds a regression test, and updates testTensorArrayWriteWrongIndexOrDataTypeFails
to expect the new negative-index error message.

[StableHLO] Fix mutation of `inputs` in `stablehlo.scatter` op interpreter

The `inputs` operand of the `stablehlo.scatter` op was getting modified by the interpreter. This is wrong behavior because SSA values are immutable.

The reason this was happening was because both `results` and `inputs` were pointing to the same data within the interpreter and thus `inputs` was getting modified when `results` was computed.

We fix that by introducing a new `clone()` function for Tensor's and using it to initialize `results`.

PR #44664: [XLA:GPU] Run PJRT buffer teardown after thunk execution

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44664

📝 Summary of Changes
Split the PJRT GPU RunAsync execution status handling so buffer teardown still runs after ExecuteWithBufferAllocations returns an error.

Add support for the `includes` feature to Windows MSVC toolchains.

This change aligns the Windows MSVC toolchains with Unix toolchains by adding support for the `includes` feature (which allows force-including headers).

Technical Details:
To support this feature on Windows, the compiler flag and the include path variable must be combined into a single argument: `"/FI%{includes}"` instead of separate arguments `["/FI", "%{includes}"]`.

When Bazel generates a compilation action on Windows, it writes compiler arguments to a parameter file (`.params`). If the flag and its value are separate elements, Bazel writes them on separate lines:
```
/FI
bazel-out/path/to/header.h
```
`clang-cl` does not support this separate-line format for `/FI` inside parameter files, causing the compilation to fail with `clang-cl: error: argument to '/FI' is missing (expected 1 value)`. Combining them into a single string forces Bazel to write them on a single line: `/FIbazel-out/path/to/header.h`, which resolves the issue.
